{{Short description|Property in descriptive set theory}}
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[descriptive set theory]], a [[subset]] of a [[Polish space]] has the '''perfect set property''' if it is either [[countable set|countable]] or has a [[empty set|nonempty]] [[perfect set|perfect]] subset.{{sfnp|Kechris|1995|p=150}} Note that having the perfect set property is not the same as being a [[perfect set]].

As nonempty perfect sets in a Polish space always have the [[cardinality of the continuum]], and the [[real number|real]]s form a Polish space, a set of reals with the perfect set property cannot be a [[counterexample]] to the [[continuum hypothesis]] (stated in the form that every [[uncountable set]] of reals has the cardinality of the continuum).

The '''Cantor–Bendixson theorem''' states that [[closed set]]s of a Polish space <math>X</math> have the perfect set property in a particularly strong form: any closed subset of <math>X</math> can be written uniquely as the [[disjoint union]] of a perfect set and a countable set.  In particular, every uncountable Polish space has the perfect set property, and can be written as the disjoint union of a perfect set and a countable [[open set]].

As a consequence, if a subset <math>S \subseteq X</math> of a Polish space <math>X</math> is such that its [[Derived set (mathematics)|derived sets]] eventually reach the empty set, that is, <math>S^{(\alpha)} = \varnothing</math> for some ordinal <math>\alpha</math>, then <math>S</math> is countable.

The [[axiom of choice]] implies the existence of sets of reals that do not have the perfect set property, such as [[Bernstein set]]s. However, in [[Solovay's model]], which satisfies all axioms of [[Zermelo Fraenkel set theory|ZF]] but not the axiom of choice, every set of reals has the perfect set property, so the use of the axiom of choice is necessary.  Every [[analytic set]] has the perfect set property.  It follows from the existence of sufficiently [[large cardinal]]s that every [[projective set]] has the perfect set property.

== Generalizations ==

Let <math>\omega_1</math> be the least uncountable [[ordinal number|ordinal]]. In an analog of [[Baire space]] derived from the <math>\omega_1</math>-fold [[Cartesian product]] of <math>\omega_1</math> with itself, any closed set is the disjoint union of an <math>\omega_1</math>-perfect set and a set of [[cardinality]] <math>\leq\aleph_1</math>, where <math>\omega_1</math>-closedness of a set is defined via a [[topological game]] in which members of <math>\omega_1^{\omega_1}</math> are played.{{sfnp|Väänänen|1991}}
